axes.question: Are there enough observations, densely enough covered, to answer at all?
Can a single dominant direction be named for the window?
How consistently does the dominant direction hold across steps?
Over how much of the window does it hold?
Does the series alternate on a short period rather than travel?
Does an established direction invert materially before the window ends?
Is step-level variation large relative to net movement?

semantics.concept: Persistence measures whether a directional tendency, once present, is SUSTAINED across the observation window despite bounded interruption. It is a statement about the window that was supplied, never a prediction.
semantics.persistentDefinition: A single dominant step direction holds across the window, interruptions are bounded (no opposing run longer than the candidate allows), and the window's net movement is consistent with that direction.
semantics.notPersistentDefinition: The window carries enough observations to judge, and no sustained tendency is present. This INCLUDES a flat series (no tendency to sustain), an oscillating or alternating series (a tendency exists but inverts every step, so it is not sustained), a zero-mean noisy series, and a series whose established direction reverses materially before the window ends.
semantics.insufficientEvidenceDefinition: The window does not carry enough observations to judge: fewer than the minimum sample count, or history coverage below the required density. DATA SUFFICIENCY ONLY.
semantics.reversalTreatment: A material reversal inside the window is NOT_PERSISTENT, because the tendency was not sustained to the window's end.
semantics.coreRule: DIRECTION_CERTAINTY and DATA_SUFFICIENCY are different axes. "No stable direction" measured over an adequate window is a POSITIVE FINDING of NOT_PERSISTENT, not an admission that the question could not be answered.
derivedFrom: STAGE2I2 head: abstains on values.length < 6 and on nothing else; a zero-signed slope answers NOT_PERSISTENT.
STAGE2I3 head: its own abstentionReason vocabulary separates SHORT_OR_MISSING_HISTORY from INDETERMINATE_DIRECTION and CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE, marking only the first as a sufficiency failure.
src/experts/oracle.js contract: "when history is too short the expert says so through ORACLE_INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY" — abstention is defined as a history-length concept.
STAGE2I4 assembly: carries a dedicated `abstention` head whose declared role is to be the sufficiency mechanism, which a second in-head sufficiency gate duplicates.
STAGE2L1/2L2/2L4 label schemas: declare a two-label persistence vocabulary with no INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE member.
semantics.notDerivedFrom: No benchmark accuracy figure was consulted in choosing this definition. The definition was fixed before any post-repair accuracy was computed.

cases.rationale: Ample data; there is no tendency at all to sustain, which is a finding, not a gap.
Direction inverts every step. Not sustained.
Large amplitude does not make an inverting series sustained.
Zero-mean noise; net movement is nil.
Every step moves the same way. Weak is not the same as unsustained.
Flat steps interleave with rises but nothing opposes the direction.
One excursion is a bounded interruption, which the contract explicitly tolerates.
The tendency was real and then was not sustained to the window end.
Direction turns repeatedly inside the window.
A cycle is the canonical sustained-nothing case.
Decaying amplitude still never sustains a direction.
Growing amplitude is a volatility statement, not a persistence one.
At the minimum the window is sufficient, so an answer is owed.
Below the minimum the window genuinely cannot support an answer. This is the ONLY legitimate abstention in the whole table.
